newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - Undaunted by arb cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - Undaunted by arb cargoes.

text.p: Asia is expected to absorb the onslaught of arbitrage gas oil cargoes without undermining prices as the regions's demand picks up and refinery shutdown for maintenance, traders said on Monday.
They said more arbitrage cargoes were expected to arrive in the Far East market this week after the Asia/Europe spread widened on Friday to $35 per tonne in favour of Asia.

Chinese traders said the mainland was expected to buy more fuel oil as domestic refiners boost gas oil production at the expense of fuel oil. Domestic inventories for gas oil were also higher than fuel oil.
Traders said China was not expected to take a back seat for too long as harvesting starts in earnest in April, increasing demand for both gas oil and fuel oil.

On the light end of the barrel, traders are awaiting results of the Saudi Aramco's import tender to buy up to 1.5 million barrels of 95 octane leaded gasoline in April. The tender closed March 4 but is valid until March 12.
Gas oil prices rose more than $2.00 per barrel last week after a local buyer purchased more than 740,000 barrels to cover requirements for China, Indonesia and Vietnam, causing the spread to widen.
Already more than 500,000 tonnes of gas oil, scheduled to arrive by early April, were being put together by several traders for shipment to East Asia and India.
But traders were undaunted. "I think these cargoes would be easily absorbed," said one trader. "We are also entering the turnaround season."
While the market was anticipating more supplies from the west, the local trader who had purchased more than 740,000 barrels of gas oil this week was expected to buy more supplies.
He already has a paper position covering more than two million barrels, traders said. The trader would not comment on the deals.
In the fuel oil market, traders were anticipating Chinese demand to pick up after a sluggish month in February.
But the market is expected to be tight with Taiwan recent purchase of 500,000 barrels, taking away some length in the market.

In Singapore, Mobil 280,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery will but shut starting March 15 for a month. Singapore Refining Company crude distillation unit one, an 18,000-bpd hydrocracker and a 32,000-bpd visbreaker remained shut. The turnaround would last until late March.

In China, Zhenhai's 75,000-bpd crude unit will also be down in March. Refinery turnarounds season in Japan and South Korea will mostly kick off in April and May. This will cause North Asia importers to cover ahead of the shutdowns, boosting prices further, traders said.
